description: Students explore the complex relationship between race, gender and labor in American literature. Questions students are invited to consider include the following: what types of labor are represented in American literature and why? Whose labor gets valued or acknowledged? What does an American laborer look like--and what does this all have to do with literature? Students also examine the construction of racialized and gendered identities as they intersect and overlap with labor issues in American literature. Genres explored include fiction, poetry and prose."
